title: apply writes a kb/_self aliases row for a rules finding that names a word pair
goal: learn records on a rules finding the word pair a miss shows (a key word of the question no passage holds, beside the word the answering line uses for it, when the reader quoted a line), and apply writes it as a kb/_self/_retrieval/aliases.csv row kept only when rag.py eval --root _self passes and the pair is in no alias file yet; a finding without such a pair stays open for a person as now

run:
import sys
try:
    import csv, hashlib, json, shutil, tempfile
    from pathlib import Path
    sys.path.insert(0, "_tools")
    import ql_apply, ql_learn, ql_store
    real = Path("kb/_self/_retrieval/aliases.csv")
    before = hashlib.sha256(real.read_bytes()).hexdigest()
    tmp = Path(tempfile.mkdtemp())
    try:
        store = tmp / "store"
        run = "20261006T000000Z-deadbeef"
        # a rules miss: the question's key word "unsaved" is in no passage, the reader quoted the line that says "uncommitted"
        entry = {"id": "E-rulespair", "root": "_self", "verdict": "weak", "route": "miss",
                 "question": "what does backlog.py land refuse when a file has unsaved changes",
                 "answer_lines": ["kb/_self/backlog.md:160"], "key_missing": ["unsaved"]}
        line = Path("kb/_self/backlog.md").read_text(encoding="utf-8").splitlines()[159]
        assert "uncommitted" in line, "fixture line moved"
        p = ql_store.run_path(store, run)
        ql_store.write_text(p, ql_store.json_lines([ql_store.header(run, {"entries": 1}), entry]))
        ql_learn.learn(store=store, rules_pack=lambda q: {"verdict": "weak", "known": False}, out=lambda *a: None)
        found = [r for r in ql_store.finding_states(store).values() if r.get("kind") == "rules"]
        assert found, "learn made no rules finding"
        pair_in_finding = "unsaved" in json.dumps(found[0]["observed"]) and "uncommitted" in json.dumps(found[0]["observed"])

        class TmpGate(ql_apply.Gate):  # the eval file and the aliases file of the rules root go into the temp dir
            def rules_eval(self):
                return tmp / "lookup_eval.csv"
        shutil.copy("kb/_self/_retrieval/lookup_eval.csv", tmp / "lookup_eval.csv")
        gate = TmpGate()
        gate.rules_aliases = lambda: tmp / "aliases.csv"  # the name a delivering change may use; ignored today
        ql_apply.apply(store=store, gate=gate, out=lambda *a: None)
        rows = [r for f in tmp.rglob("*.csv") if f.name != "lookup_eval.csv" for r in csv.reader(open(f, encoding="utf-8"))]
        in_alias = any(len(r) > 1 and "unsaved" in r[0].lower() and "uncommitted" in r[1].lower() for r in rows)
        after = hashlib.sha256(real.read_bytes()).hexdigest()
        assert before == after, "real aliases.csv was touched"
        ok = pair_in_finding and in_alias
        print("%s: pair recorded on the finding=%s; alias row (unsaved,uncommitted) written=%s" % ("ok" if ok else "FAIL", pair_in_finding, in_alias))
        sys.exit(0 if ok else 1)
    finally:
        shutil.rmtree(tmp, ignore_errors=True)
except SystemExit:
    raise
except Exception as e:
    print("check error", repr(e))
    sys.exit(1)

notes: Planning 2026-10-06: the planted check builds a store in a temporary directory with one _self miss quoting kb/_self/backlog.md's 'uncommitted' line, runs ql_learn.learn and ql_apply.apply on it and asks for the pair on the finding's observed field and an alias row with both words in the temporary directory; it also checks that the real kb/_self/_retrieval/aliases.csv is unchanged. Gate.targets (ql_apply.py) has no aliases path for a _self rules finding today; the check sets a gate.rules_aliases attribute as the hook it expects, which the worker may rename with the check.
